Science.summary: Soil respiration (Rs), the efflux of CO₂ from soils to the atmosphere driven by root and microbial activity, is one of the largest terrestrial carbon fluxes and a primary determinant of net carbon sequestration. The important role of nitrogen in driving terrestrial carbon sequestration has long been recognized. However, the role of nitrogen in the temporal dynamics of Rs has not been well understood.

Science.title: 'Arrival' at 10: Denis Villeneuve's alien visitation classic that reminded us it's good to talk
Science.summary: How the 'Dune' director turned a little-known short story into one of the best sci-fi movies of the 21st century

Science.title: Same farms, different answers: When nitrogen pollution estimates don't add up
Science.summary: To reduce nitrogen pollution stemming from synthetic fertilizer and livestock waste, California's Central Valley relies on five data sets to estimate surplus nitrogen. However, most parts of the United States use just one or two data sets—the U.S. Department of Agriculture's agricultural survey and census—to estimate nitrogen surplus.

Science.title: Kindergarten teachers offer cognitive help during outdoor play but fall short on emotional and social support
Science.summary: A study in the International Journal of Innovation and Sustainable Development of teachers' behavior during outdoor play at kindergarten has identified a gap between the support children need and the help educators provide, particularly in emotional and social development.

Science.title: A likely supermassive neutron star might shed light on the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes
Science.summary: A team of astronomers recently identified a red giant star with an unseen binary companion after examining data from the Large Sky Area MultiObject Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE). Although the companion object can't be observed visually, astronomers can see the gravitational effects it has on the red giant star.

Science.title: Water-activated polymer forms solid shapes underwater and bonds glass fragments
Science.summary: Cement hardens when mixed with water, allowing it to form solid structures even in wet environments. This property is known as hydraulicity. Reproducing this property in organic polymers has been challenging, as polymer materials that react with moisture often lack the combination of bulk curing and water resistance needed to harden reliably in wet conditions.

Science.title: Combining five metals in one oxide improves ethanol gas sensing
Science.summary: A technology that significantly improves ethanol gas sensing performance by combining five different metal elements in a single oxide has been developed.

Science.title: Who lives in a sponge under the sea? Tiny Caribbean fish and their microscopic neighbors
Science.summary: Two new studies involving Newcastle University marine scientist Dr. Theresa Rueger have highlighted how the tusked goby's relationship with its host sponge shapes almost every aspect of its life. Rueger, a senior lecturer in tropical marine sciences at Newcastle University's School of Natural and Environmental Sciences, is senior author of one study and co-author of the other, which together uncover the influence of sponges on the tiny Caribbean reef fish's social behavior, growth, reproduction and microbiome.

Science.title: This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star
Science.summary: A hidden black hole or neutron star companion to an unstable massive star is causing the system to erupt in light that mimics a supernova explosion.

Science.title: Rh₃ clusters balance activity and butene selectivity in butane dehydrogenation
Science.summary: Scientists from the Institute of Metal Research (IMR) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, in collaboration with researchers from Peking University and Chongqing University, have demonstrated how the geometry and electronic properties of subnanometer rhodium (Rh) active sites shape C–H activation, product desorption and C–C bond cleavage during butane dehydrogenation.

Science.title: Fruit fly sleep protein yields peptides that inhibit drug-resistant bacteria in lab tests
Science.summary: Researchers at University of Tsukuba and collaborating institutions have identified short antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri, a sleep-inducing protein in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster. The research is published in the journal Nature Communications.

Science.title: Astronomers confirm a tiny new moon is orbiting Earth, and it'll stick around for the holidays
Science.summary: A tiny asteroid entered Earth's orbit in April and is expected to leave in January. Meet the minimoon 2026 QQ8.

Science.title: A widely used antibiotic for acne and infections is linked to risk of pregnancy loss, new study finds
Science.summary: A common antibiotic may be linked to a higher risk of miscarriage and stillbirth when used early in pregnancy, a new study suggests.

Science.summary: This Vampire Survivors spin-off has a lot of love for the famous grimdark sci-fi universe, but without the intimidatingly dense lore and complex systems.
